full_judgment: 2. The facts involved for disposal of the Rule are as follows : The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 being the plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 11 of 1986 in the Court of Munsif, Rupganj Thana against the petitioners and others for redemption of mortgaged property and for giving delivery of possession of the mortgaged land, asserting, inter alia, that the land measuring 38 decimals comprising plot No. 309 under Khatian No. 256 Mouza Khadn originally belonged to Hossain Baksh who took a loan of Taka 80 from Abdul Jabber and mortgage deed executed on 23-12-1924 and 16-2-1925 and that it was stipulated in the said deed that the mortgagee Abdul Jabber will possess and enjoy the land on account of interest on the money paid and that Hossain Baksh will get the mortgaged land redeemed on payment of the mortgagee money within the month of Falgun, 1334 BS in default, Abdul Jabber will possess the land until the money is paid and that in the event of non payment of money at a time the mortgagee Abdul Jabber Prodhan will be at liberty to realise the money by selling land through the Court. Hossain Baksh died after two years from the date of mortgage, "leaving behind wife Kbadija Bibi, two daughters Aku 'Bibi and Gedi Bibi and one brother, namely, Abdul Karim, and thereafter Khadija Bibi died leaving two daughters as aforesaid and that after the death of Hossain Baksh, his two daughters tried to repay their father's loan to Abdul Jabber but Abdul Jabber being actuated by greed did not accept the money offered and as a result the daughters of Hossain Baksh had not been able to redeem the suit land. Abdul Jabbar died leaving behind four sons and two daughters, the defendant Nos. 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 and thereafter son Abdur Rahim died leaving his son, the defendant No. 6 and two daughters, the defendant Nos. 7 and 8 and that the heirs of Hossain Baksh requested the heirs of Abdul Jabbar to return the mortgaged loan on receiving the money put to no effect. Aku Bibi, the daughter of Hossain Baksh, died leaving the plaintiff and the plaintiff requested the defendant Nos. 1-3, the heirs of Abdul Jabber, to release the mortgaged land on acceptance of the money in the 1st part of the month of Ashwin, 1342 BS when the said defendants disclosed that the suit land is in possession of the defendant No.9 and. as such, they have no right to accept the mortgaged money and to deliver possession of the land and that the plaintiff also requested the defendant No. 9 to accept the money and surrender possession of the land but the defendant refused to do so and hence the suit.
